hypotheses.claim: With only one archived solver (mean objective 27.5278, 0.62 ms mean solve, no time pressure at all against the 500 ms budget), the bottleneck is packing quality, not speed. Claim: replacing a plain descending-size priority with a score of the form score_item = size (primary) + lambda * (fractional residual penalty) and switching the repack insertion rule from first-fit to best-fit-style placement over the reordered list will reduce bin count on the size=200 regime (vbs_mean 46.4167, currently the deepest objective scale) by at least 1 bin on average, i.e. mean objective under 27.5278, while remaining far inside the time budget (expected < 5 ms/instance). Rationale: FFD on heterogeneous items leaves slack fragmentation; best-fit placement plus a residual-aware priority preserves large-item openings for later fits.

next_search_advice.direction: Strengthen the offline item-priority score so descending-size first-fit is strictly dominated: rank items by a size-dominant score combined with a residual-fit-aware tie-break, then repack into the first bin whose remaining capacity matches the item best (best-fit-decreasing style placement over the reordered sequence).
